audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers score the chart Rumble / Rumble / Rumble / Rumble / Skill / Rumble / Rumble at a 54.45% Darius win rate, while the entry's own whys[0]-[3] say 'Level 1 favours Darius', 'Level 2 favours Darius', 'Level 3 favours Darius', 'Levels 4-5 favour Darius', content.early says 'Levels 1-4 are firmly yours' and whys[5]/[6] call first item and 2+ items skill windows.
audit.why: Every prose field in the entry says the opposite of the chart it sits next to. The Darius packet chart reads Darius/Darius/Darius/Darius/Rumble/Skill/Skill and the Rumble-side packet chart reads Darius/Darius/Skill/Skill/Rumble/Skill/Skill; the two agree on levels 1-2 (Darius), level 6 (Rumble) and both item stages (Skill), and disagree only at levels 3 and 4-5. Levels 3-5 are genuinely contested — Danger Zone Flamespitter matches Darius's bleed and two Electro Harpoon charges at 850 range kite a 535-range pull — so Skill is the reading both sides can hold.
audit.corrected: Darius / Darius / Skill / Skill / Rumble / Skill / Skill in both layers, matching the already-written Rumble-side audit (audits/top/rumble__darius.json) so the mirror does not fight.
sources: internal contradiction with whys[0]-[3] and content.early

audit.whatIsWrong: The Level 6 phase text carries the LaTeX fragment 'R = d + a \times Stacks'. Rumble's spikes are written as 'Scrap Shield online, level 6, first item' with no numbers, and spikes[0] tells you to trade 'while his shield is on cooldown'.
audit.why: Scrap Shield is a flat 6 seconds at every rank — it is never meaningfully on cooldown, so an entire trading rule is built on a window that does not exist. The real Rumble spike is Heat: Danger Zone at 50% empowers all three basics. Flamespitter is 10s falling to 6s and The Equalizer is 130/105/80 — those are the numbers that decide when you commit.
audit.corrected: Plain-language Level 6 text; Danger Zone named as the spike; Scrap Shield's 6s, Flamespitter's 10s and Equalizer's 130s written in.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry never mentions that Electro Harpoon reduces Magic Resist, never gives a range for anything, and describes Overheat only as '(silence)'. focus, loading, dosFull[0], report[5] and breakdown.cooldowns all tell you to track and bait Scrap Shield.
audit.why: Riot's text: Electro Harpoon 'slowing their Move Speed, and reducing their Magic Resist', 850 range, two charges. Flamespitter is a 600-range cone burning for 3 seconds. Apprehend is 535 — so Rumble out-ranges your only engage with both damage abilities, which is the whole shape of the lane and the entry never says it. Overheat is not a silence: Riot's text is 'gaining bonus Attack Speed and granting his basic attacks bonus damage, but making him unable to cast spells for a few seconds' — he gets stronger in melee while it lasts, so you all-in with the pull, not by trading autos.
audit.corrected: Ranges 850/600/535 stated, MR shred named, Overheat described accurately, and the tracked ability moved from Scrap Shield to the Heat bar.

audit.why: Flamespitter and Electro Harpoon both deal magic damage and Electro Harpoon additionally shreds your MR, so armour boots are the wrong buy in this specific matchup.
audit.corrected: Mercury's Treads named for this matchup.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns is a PDF-extraction run-on ending in the page artefact '• • Darius Top Lane Matchup Database 58' and calls Scrap Shield 'matchup-defining'.
audit.why: The punishable cooldowns are Flamespitter (10s to 6s) and The Equalizer (130s at rank 1); Scrap Shield's 6s is not punishable, and Apprehend's 26s at rank 1 is the cooldown you are actually protecting.
audit.corrected: Rewritten with the real numbers and the page artefact removed.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing says The Equalizer does not block movement.
audit.why: The derived kit flags tag The Equalizer and Scrap Shield with 'terrain' and Scrap Shield with 'knockup'. Riot's own descriptions carry none of that — Scrap Shield is a shield plus a speed burst, and The Equalizer 'damages and slows'. If a player believes the ult walls him off he will not walk through it, which is exactly what he should do.
audit.corrected: Equalizer stated as a damaging, slowing line you walk sideways out of.

Darius Ghost: hold it to cross the Equalizer line.

edits.after: Post-6 it's skill-driven — Stridebreaker forces him off his spacing and 54.45% says you usually win, but a Rumble who kites on Scrap Shield's speed and holds a 130s Equalizer trades evenly. Land Apprehend and it's yours; miss and his burn wins.

notes: Kit-flag false positives confirmed independently of the Rumble-side audit: rumble.json tags Scrap Shield with 'knockup' and 'terrain' and The Equalizer with 'terrain'. Riot's descriptions carry none of it (Scrap Shield is a shield plus a speed burst; The Equalizer 'damages and slows'). The _missing entry 'Both sides carry displacement (Apprehend (E) vs Scrap Shield (W))' rests entirely on that bad flag and was NOT written into the matchup. Win-rate mismatch worth someone's attention: the Darius packet reports this matchup at 54.45% over 1078 games while the Rumble packet reports the same matchup at 49.56% over 1485 games — the two tables do not sum to 100 and were clearly sampled differently. breakdown.wave and breakdown.trading carry the same PDF-extraction run-on flagged on the garen, gnar and riven entries; left untouched for consistency. diff is the enum 'EVEN' at diffRating 7/10 on a 54.45% win rate — arguably too harsh, but I did not churn it.
